# PART 66 – CROWN PROCEEDINGS

[PART 66 – CROWN PROCEEDINGS] Contents of this Part

[PART 66 – CROWN PROCEEDINGS] Title | Number

[PART 66 – CROWN PROCEEDINGS] Scope of this Part and interpretation | Rule 66.1

[PART 66 – CROWN PROCEEDINGS] Application of the Civil Procedure Rules | Rule 66.2

[PART 66 – CROWN PROCEEDINGS] Action on behalf of the Crown | Rule 66.3

[PART 66 – CROWN PROCEEDINGS] Counterclaims, other additional claims, and set-off | Rule 66.4

[PART 66 – CROWN PROCEEDINGS] Applications in revenue matters | Rule 66.5

[PART 66 – CROWN PROCEEDINGS] Enforcement against the Crown | Rule 66.6

[PART 66 – CROWN PROCEEDINGS] Money due from the Crown | Rule 66.7

## Scope of this Part and interpretation

## 66.1

[PART 66 – CROWN PROCEEDINGS > 66.1] (1) This Part contains rules for civil proceedings by or against the Crown, and other civil proceedings to which the Crown is a party.

[PART 66 – CROWN PROCEEDINGS > 66.1] (2) In this Part –

[PART 66 – CROWN PROCEEDINGS > 66.1] (a) ‘the Act’ means the Crown Proceedings Act 1947;

[PART 66 – CROWN PROCEEDINGS > 66.1] (b) ‘civil proceedings by the Crown’ means the civil proceedings described in section 23(1) of the Act, but excluding the proceedings described in section 23(3);

[PART 66 – CROWN PROCEEDINGS > 66.1] (c) ‘civil proceedings against the Crown’ means the civil proceedings described in section 23(2) of the Act, but excluding the proceedings described in section 23(3);

[PART 66 – CROWN PROCEEDINGS > 66.1] (d) ‘civil proceedings to which the Crown is a party’ has the same meaning as it has for the purposes of Parts III and IV of the Act by virtue of section 38(4).

## Application of the Civil Procedure Rules

## 66.2

[PART 66 – CROWN PROCEEDINGS > 66.2] These Rules and their practice directions apply to civil proceedings by or against the Crown and to other civil proceedings to which the Crown is a party unless this Part, a practice direction or any other enactment provides otherwise.

## Action on behalf of the Crown

## 66.3

[PART 66 – CROWN PROCEEDINGS > 66.3] (1) Where by reason of a rule, practice direction or court order the Crown is permitted or required –

[PART 66 – CROWN PROCEEDINGS > 66.3] (a) to make a witness statement,

[PART 66 – CROWN PROCEEDINGS > 66.3] (b) to swear an affidavit,

[PART 66 – CROWN PROCEEDINGS > 66.3] (c) to verify a document by a statement of truth;

[PART 66 – CROWN PROCEEDINGS > 66.3] (d) to make a disclosure statement; or

[PART 66 – CROWN PROCEEDINGS > 66.3] (e) to discharge any other procedural obligation,

[PART 66 – CROWN PROCEEDINGS > 66.3] that function shall be performed by an appropriate officer acting on behalf of the Crown.

[PART 66 – CROWN PROCEEDINGS > 66.3] (2) The court may if necessary nominate an appropriate officer.

## Counterclaims, other additional claims, and set-off

## 66.4

[PART 66 – CROWN PROCEEDINGS > 66.4] (1) In a claim by the Crown for taxes, duties or penalties, the defendant cannot make a counterclaim or other additional claim or raise a defence of set-off.

[PART 66 – CROWN PROCEEDINGS > 66.4] (2) In any other claim by the Crown, the defendant cannot make a counterclaim or other additional claim or raise a defence of set-off which is based on a claim for repayment of taxes, duties or penalties.

[PART 66 – CROWN PROCEEDINGS > 66.4] (3) In proceedings by or against the Crown in the name of the Attorney-General, no counterclaim or other additional claim can be made or defence of set-off raised without the permission of the court.

[PART 66 – CROWN PROCEEDINGS > 66.4] (4) In proceedings by or against the Crown in the name of a government department, no counterclaim or other additional claim can be made or defence of set-off raised without the permission of the court unless the subject-matter relates to that government department.

## Applications in revenue matters

## 66.5

[PART 66 – CROWN PROCEEDINGS > 66.5] (1) This rule sets out the procedure under section 14 of the Act, which allows the Crown to make summary applications in the High Court in certain revenue matters.

[PART 66 – CROWN PROCEEDINGS > 66.5] (2) The application must be made in the High Court using the Part 8 procedure.

[PART 66 – CROWN PROCEEDINGS > 66.5] (3) The title of the claim form must clearly identify the matters which give rise to the application.

## Enforcement against the Crown

## 66.6

[PART 66 – CROWN PROCEEDINGS > 66.6] (1) The following rules do not apply to any order against the Crown –

[PART 66 – CROWN PROCEEDINGS > 66.6] (a) Rules 40.8A and 70.2A and Parts 69 to 73, 81, 83, 84 and 89; and;

[PART 66 – CROWN PROCEEDINGS > 66.6] (b) Omitted

[PART 66 – CROWN PROCEEDINGS > 66.6] (c) CCR Order 28.

[PART 66 – CROWN PROCEEDINGS > 66.6] (2) In paragraph (1), ‘order against the Crown’ means any judgment or order against the Crown, a government department, or an officer of the Crown as such, made –

[PART 66 – CROWN PROCEEDINGS > 66.6] (a) in civil proceedings by or against the Crown;

[PART 66 – CROWN PROCEEDINGS > 66.6] (b) in proceedings in the Administrative Court;

[PART 66 – CROWN PROCEEDINGS > 66.6] (c) in connection with an arbitration to which the Crown is a party; or

[PART 66 – CROWN PROCEEDINGS > 66.6] (d) in other civil proceedings to which the Crown is a party.

[PART 66 – CROWN PROCEEDINGS > 66.6] (3) An application under section 25(1) of the Act for a separate certificate of costs payable to the applicant may be made without notice.

## Money due from the Crown

## 66.7

[PART 66 – CROWN PROCEEDINGS > 66.7] (1) None of the following orders –

[PART 66 – CROWN PROCEEDINGS > 66.7] (a) a third party debt order under Part 72;

[PART 66 – CROWN PROCEEDINGS > 66.7] (b) an order for the appointment of a receiver under Part 69; or

[PART 66 – CROWN PROCEEDINGS > 66.7] (c) an order for the appointment of a sequestrator under RSC Order 45,

[PART 66 – CROWN PROCEEDINGS > 66.7] may be made or have effect in respect of any money due from the Crown.

[PART 66 – CROWN PROCEEDINGS > 66.7] (2) In paragraph (1), ‘money due from the Crown’ includes money accruing due, and money alleged to be due or accruing due.

[PART 66 – CROWN PROCEEDINGS > 66.7] (3) An application for an order under section 27 of the Act –

[PART 66 – CROWN PROCEEDINGS > 66.7] (a) restraining a person from receiving money payable to him by the Crown; and

[PART 66 – CROWN PROCEEDINGS > 66.7] (b) directing payment of the money to the applicant or another person,

[PART 66 – CROWN PROCEEDINGS > 66.7] may be made under Part 23.

[PART 66 – CROWN PROCEEDINGS > 66.7] (4) The application must be supported by written evidence setting out the facts on which it is based, and in particular identifying the debt from the Crown.

[PART 66 – CROWN PROCEEDINGS > 66.7] (5) Where the debt from the Crown is money in a National Savings Bank account, the witness must if possible identify the number of the account and the name and address of the branch where it is held.

[PART 66 – CROWN PROCEEDINGS > 66.7] (6) Notice of the application, with a copy of the written evidence, must be served –

[PART 66 – CROWN PROCEEDINGS > 66.7] (a) on the Crown, and

[PART 66 – CROWN PROCEEDINGS > 66.7] (b) on the person to be restrained,

[PART 66 – CROWN PROCEEDINGS > 66.7] at least 7 days before the hearing.

[PART 66 – CROWN PROCEEDINGS > 66.7] (7) Rule 72.8 applies to an application under this rule as it applies to an application under rule 72.2 for a third party debt order, except that the court will not have the power to order enforcement to issue against the Crown.
